en.askTitle: Put in your own sales, bills and cash to get a 13-week cash forecast that shows the weeks you would run short
en.runTitle: A one-location US coffee shop: a 13-week cash forecast that rolls forward in ten minutes a week

fields.label: Country or state, currency and business type
fields.value: A single-location coffee shop in the US, in US dollars

fields.label: Cash on hand, tax reserve and minimum buffer
fields.placeholder: e.g. $18,000 in the bank, $4,000 of it set aside for taxes, keep at least $5,000 spendable

fields.label: Card sales history, unsettled cards, processor cut-off and fees
fields.value: About $38,000 in monthly sales, higher on weekends and in winter

fields.label: Supplier bills, catering, payroll, rent, loan, taxes and owner draws
fields.value: Six part-time staff paid biweekly; rent $6,500 due on the 1st; a $40k SBA loan being repaid; quarterly estimated taxes; suppliers paid on net-15 and net-30

en.template: Adapt this 13-week cash workbook for my café in {where}, starting Monday {start}, using {cash}, {pos}, {bills}. Keep facts and assumptions separate, formulas and tab names intact, and replace estimates without duplicates. Show baseline and {drop} weekly flows, cash, reserve, spendable cash and daily lows; keep commitments fixed unless changed. Do not invent finance or equate positive cash with profit/solvency or reserves with tax owed. Test zero-drop, roll-forward, holidays, overdue and negative-cash cases on copies, flag range limits, and keep records local without uploads, contact or transactions.

phases.title: Confirm public benchmarks and plan the dated cash schedules
Build the Excel forecast and the one-page update guide
phases.note: Card payout delays, catering, payroll weeks, rent, supplier terms, loan and tax set-asides
phases.judgment: It did not dress up a benchmark as a target. The 32.4% supplier-cost figure comes from a broad survey of limited-service restaurants, not coffee shops specifically, and the workbook says it is only a rough proxy for the supplier budget.

phases.title: Recalculate, test sales-drop and roll-forward cases, and check the delivery
phases.note: Every formula recalculated and the weekly roll-forward tested
phases.judgment: While testing the roll-forward it added a warning for overdue unpaid bills, so they can’t silently drop out when the start date moves on. The finished example also shows the user’s real problem: total cash rises slightly in week one, yet spendable cash dips to $4,656, under the $5,000 floor.

workers: Wrote the one-page, ten-minute weekly guide for a shop owner who is not an accountant

zh.askTitle: 填上你自己的销售、账单和现金，得到一份能看出哪几周会缺钱的 13 周现金预测
zh.runTitle: 美国一家单店咖啡馆：每周只花十分钟就能滚动更新的 13 周现金预测

fields.label: 国家或州、币种和主体类型
fields.value: 美国的一家单店咖啡馆，用美元

fields.label: 预测起始的第一个周一
fields.placeholder: 例如：2026 年 11 月 9 日（周一）

fields.label: 现有现金、税款储备和最低缓冲
fields.placeholder: 例如：账上 1.8 万美元，其中 4,000 美元留作税款，至少保持 5,000 美元可动用

fields.label: 刷卡销售历史、未结算刷卡款、处理商截止时间和费用
fields.value: 月销售额约 3.8 万美元，周末和冬天更高

fields.label: 供应商账单、外烩、工资、房租、贷款、税款和店主提款
fields.value: 6 名兼职员工，双周发薪；房租每月 1 号 6,500 美元；还着一笔 4 万美元的 SBA 贷款；按季预缴税；供应商账期 15 天和 30 天

zh.template: 请为{where}咖啡馆，从{start}周一起调整这份 13 周表，用{cash}、{pos}、{bills}。事实假设分开，保留公式和表名，替换估算不重复；展示基准及{drop}每周进出、现金、储备、可用额和每日低点，承诺成本未经更改保持固定。不编融资，不把正现金当盈利或偿债能力，也不把储备当税额。在副本试零降幅、滚动、假日、逾期和负现金，提示范围限制；仅本地使用，不上传、联系或交易。

phases.title: 确认公开的行业参考数据，并设计带日期的收支安排
做出 Excel 预测表和一页纸更新指南
phases.note: 刷卡到账延迟、外烩、发薪周、房租、供应商账期、贷款和税款预留
phases.judgment: 它没有把行业参考数据包装成目标。32.4% 的供应成本比例来自对快餐类餐厅的宽口径调查，不是专门针对咖啡馆，表格里也写明它只是粗略参考。

phases.title: 重算全部公式，测试销售下降和滚动更新，并检查交付
phases.note: 所有公式重新计算，每周滚动更新也测试过
phases.judgment: 测试滚动更新时，它加了一条“逾期未付账单”提醒，免得起始日期往后挪时这些账单悄悄消失。做好的示例也把用户真正的问题摆了出来：第一周总现金略有上升，可动用现金却降到 4,656 美元，低于 5,000 美元的底线。

workers: 为不是会计的店主写了一页纸、每周十分钟的更新指南
